有人问钱包怎么处理。: Someone asked what to do with the wallet.
问题是，没有人知道该寄到哪里。: The problem was nobody knew where.

前线来了一批邮件。: A batch of mail reached the front.
大部分是家里寄来的 —— 毛衣、糖、还有晒干的烟叶。: Mostly from home — sweaters, sugar, dried tobacco leaf.
邮差说，也有往家里寄的，但是寄不出去。: The postman said there was outbound mail too, but it couldn't go out.
他把一叠信封放在桌上：这都是之前阵亡的战友写的。: He set a stack of envelopes on the table: these are from men who died.
他问：要不要帮忙送？: He asked: want me to deliver them?
但他已经送了 —— 他说他每个月都自己掏钱买邮票。: But he'd been delivering them anyway — buying the stamps himself every month.
至少这个能帮。: At least this you can do.
战壕里住着一只猫。: A cat lived in the trench.
没人知道它是从哪来的。可能是从城里跑出来的。: Nobody knew where it came from. Probably ran out of the city.
士兵们把自己那份罐头分一点给它。它不挑。: The men shared their tins with it. It wasn't picky.
它只在炮击的时候躲进洞里，其他时候就蹲在沙袋上晒太阳。: It only hid during shelling. The rest of the time it sat on the sandbags in the sun.
有个兵说：它比我们命大。: One soldier said: it's got more lives than us.
另一个说：不，它只是不在乎。: Another said: no. It just doesn't care.
后来有一天，炮击之后，猫没回来。: Then one day, after a shelling, the cat didn't come back.
有人在战壕外面找了很久。: Someone searched outside the trench for a long time.
浪费时间，但你还是去了。: A waste of time, but you went anyway.
战争里死掉的东西太多了。: Too many things die in a war.
一间被炸掉半边的教室。: A classroom with half its walls blown away.
黑板还挂在墙上。上面写着：: The blackboard still hung there. It read:
下面的课桌上，散着一叠作文本。: Below, a stack of exercise books scattered across the desks.
最上面那本，翻开着。上面只写了两行：: The top one lay open. Only two lines were written:
「我的理想是当老师。因为老师可以教别人。」: "My dream is to be a teacher. Because teachers can teach others."
「可是老师说，今年可能没有暑假了。」: "But teacher said there might be no summer holiday this year."
后面的字迹被雨水泡烂了。: The rest had been ruined by rain.
那一夜，对面的枪声停了。: That night the firing from the other side stopped.
战壕里的人都醒了。有人以为要进攻，端起了枪。: Everyone in the trench woke. Some thought it was an attack and raised their rifles.
然后对面传来声音 —— 有人在唱歌。: Then sound came across — someone singing.
过了一会儿，居然有人跟着哼起来，然后是笑。: After a while someone picked up the tune. Then came laughter.
两边的战壕里都有人在笑。笑得很累，但确实在笑。: There was laughter in both trenches. Tired laughter, but real.
二十分钟后，双方都恢复了原状。: Twenty minutes later, both sides went back to normal.
第二天早上，炮击照旧。: The next morning the shelling resumed as usual.
但你记得那二十分钟。: But you remembered those twenty minutes.
那时候没有人是敌人。: For that while, nobody was an enemy.
有些事不该进档案。: Some things don't belong in the files.
你收到一个任务：把阵亡者的身份牌收集起来。: You were given a job: collect the dog tags of the dead.
有个新兵跟着你做。他做得很快，一直到某一块牌子。: A new man worked alongside you. He was quick — until one tag.
他停下来，蹲在原地很久。: He stopped and crouched there a long time.
你走过去看。牌子上是他哥哥的名字。: You went over. The name was his brother's.
他早就知道哥哥阵亡了 —— 家里写过信。: He'd known his brother was dead — the family had written.
他说：我以为已经有人捡过了。: He said: I thought someone had already picked it up.
两个人都没有动。风很大。: Neither of you moved. The wind was strong.
这种时候，多半想一个人。: Times like this, a man wants to be alone.
你走开了，回头看见他还蹲着。: You walked away and looked back. He was still crouched.
炊事班找到一罐罐头，煮了一锅汤。: The cooks found one tin and made a pot of soup.
每人一勺，正好分完。: One ladle each. It came out exact.
最后轮到一个人，锅里没了。: When it reached the last man, the pot was empty.
炊事兵愣了一下，把自己那碗递过去。: The cook hesitated, then held out his own bowl.
对方摇头，说：你比我大。: The other shook his head: you're older than me.
两个人推来推去。最后谁也没喝，把碗放在了中间。: They pushed it back and forth. In the end neither drank. The bowl sat between them.
第二天，两个人都没醒来。: The next morning, neither of them woke.
汤还在那里，冻住了。: The soup was still there. Frozen.
田野里立着一个稻草人。: A scarecrow stood in the field.
它的衣服是军装的旧布，帽子是士兵的帽子。: Its clothes were scraps of uniform. Its hat was a soldier's cap.
显然是有人把自己的东西给了一个稻草人。: Someone had clearly given their own things to a scarecrow.
不知道为什么，没有一棵庄稼。: For some reason, there were no crops at all.
也许是因为种地的人都不在了。: Maybe because the people who farmed were gone.
也许是因为，给稻草人穿衣服的人，只是想证明: Maybe because whoever dressed the scarecrow only wanted to prove
这里曾经有人生活过。: that people had once lived here.
